subject: BlueSparrow renewal — utilization-triggered H100 staging & throttling plan
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel@bluesparrow.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@bluesparrow.ai>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BlueSparrow renewal — capacity ask and utilization data

Diego / Ben —

Thanks for the run of the numbers last week. We pulled the July metrics and wanted to share the signal driving our renewal ask: overall request volume is up ~34% month-over-month, and sustained inference concurrency during our morning batch windows now sits at ~420–480 active sessions (p95 spikes to ~520). Average GPU utilization on the current H100 pool is 78% across the day and regularly breaches 90% during the 09:00–11:00 UTC window.

Key constraints from our side:
- p95 latency target must remain <= 350ms for the live API
- cannot tolerate sustained queueing that adds >50ms tail latency
- procurement prefers staged increases over a single large commit

Can Redwood propose a phased plan (short-term staging + monitoring window) that will keep p95 latency under control while we finalize our purchase order? Attached is the raw usage CSV for July and a short dashboard export.

Also open to discussing a fallback routing policy if utilization keeps hitting the 90% band — we’d prefer to avoid a full pricing re-negotiation mid-quarter.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of ML Engineering — BlueSparrow
Attachments: usage_report_July2026.csv (csv)

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <daniel@bluesparrow.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueSparrow renewal — capacity ask and utilization data

Thanks for the data, Daniel — this is helpful. High level proposal below; I attached a workbook with a few SKU mixes and cost delta scenarios (proposed_sku_plan_v3.xlsx).

Short-term (immediate 30–45 day window):
- Provision a staged canary pool of +8 H100s (isolated tenant pool) to absorb morning batch spikes.
- Routing: sticky session routing to canary pool for 20% of traffic during the 09:00–11:00 UTC window; auto-scale threshold for the canary at 65% cluster utilization.
- Observability: 60-day monitoring with daily rollups and a 7-day rolling p95 check. Automatic rollback if canary increases p95 or if utilization stays <40% for the window.

Medium-term (60–180 days):
- If 60-day window shows sustained 70%+ utilization on the expanded pool, convert +8 H100 to reserved tranche (commit) with 10% discount band.
- If utilization is bursty, maintain mixed model: reserved baseline + burst credits for ephemeral peaks.

Failover / throttling policy suggestion:
- When global p95 for the customer group exceeds 85% for >15 minutes, automatically route low-priority jobs to the 8-bit quantized variant and enable burst credits for high-priority requests.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) We’ll share a DocuSign-ready amendment (contract excerpt attached) that covers a 90-day staging clause.
2) Set up a daily 10min check-in for the first two weeks post-provisioning.
3) Assign owners: Diego (Redwood) — rollout & observability; Ben — pricing & commit options; Laura — procurement coordination.

Can you confirm PO cadence and whether BlueSparrow is comfortable with a staged 8-H100 canary?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_sku_plan_v3.xlsx (xlsx)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel@bluesparrow.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueSparrow renewal — capacity ask and utilization data

Diego / Daniel — quick add from pricing side. Two points to consider that change the economics:

1) Hybrid fleet option: mix of H100s (for latency-sensitive endpoints) + a smaller pool of lower-cost high-memory A100-L3 instances for batch inference. This reduces committed H100 hours by ~18% while preserving p95 for live traffic. See sheet 'hybrid_mix' in the workbook.

2) Staged commit trigger: rather than a fixed 60-day conversion, propose a utilization-banded trigger: if 7-day rolling avg utilization >72% AND 95th percentile sustained concurrency >400 for 10 consecutive days, convert 50% of the canary into reserved capacity. This avoids converting too early on transient spikes.

Procurement note: If BlueSparrow wants to lock pricing for the rest of FY26, we can offer a tranche-level discount (10–12%) in exchange for a minimum 6-month commit on the converted capacity. I’ll coordinate with finance once procurement confirms timeline.

cc: Karthik for operational feasibility and Laura for PO sequencing.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Deal Strategy, Redwood Inference

—Priya

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-09-02T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueSparrow renewal — capacity ask and utilization data 

Summary and agreed actions: thank you all for the quick turnaround.

Decision (agreed):
- Redwood will provision a staged canary pool of +8 H100s within 48 hours of receiving the signed amendment/PO.
- Staging duration: 90 days with a 60-day primary evaluation window and an optional 30-day extension if metrics are borderline.
- Utilization-banded commit trigger (agreed to Ben’s suggestion): convert 50% of the canary to reserved capacity if both conditions met: 7-day rolling avg utilization >72% AND 95th percentile sustained concurrency >400 for 10 consecutive days.

Operational details / owners:
- Rollout owner: Diego Fernandez (Redwood) — schedule provisioning and create isolated canary pool.
- Pricing/commit owner: Ben Carter (Redwood) — prepare commit amendment and tranche discount options.
- Procurement owner: Laura Bennett (Redwood) — coordinate DocuSign + PO matching (PO #BS-2026-334).
- Customer-side owner: Daniel Park (BlueSparrow) — enable routing for 20% canary traffic and validate latency telemetry.

Throttling & fallback:
- When p95 > 85% for >15 mins, Redwood will do two normal actions in sequence: 1) shift low-priority jobs to the quantized variant, 2) enable burst credits for priority traffic. This requires BlueSparrow to accept quantized-model fallbacks for a subset of traffic; Daniel — please confirm your engineering team can toggle that switch (we can provide a short client-side snippet).

Next steps (timeline):
- Redwood sends amendment + DocuSign link today (Laura).
- BlueSparrow to return signed amendment + PO within 7 business days if possible.
- Provisioning scheduled upon receipt; daily 10min checks for first 14 days.
- Review meeting at day 30 and day 60 (tentative calendar invites to follow).

If anyone wants to escalate a different mix (Ben’s hybrid fleet or an alternate tranche) we can run the numbers in parallel, but this gives BlueSparrow immediate headroom for the next quarter.

Action items (short):
- Laura: send DocuSign amendment (today).
- Daniel: confirm client-side fallback readiness (by EOD 2026-09-03).
- Priya: confirm procurement timeline / PO cadence (by EOD 2026-09-06).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the DocuSign link and a short runbook for the first 14 days.
